children.value: > Fact From Story: Wang and Bankman-Fried determined that about $8 billion in customer money was gone
> Fact From Story: Alameda’s lenders wanted their money back, and Bankman-Fried directed the group to pay back the lenders using FTX customer funds.
> > Fact From Story: FTX was not fine and assets were not fine because FTX did not have enough assets for customer withdrawals
> > > Fact From Story: Wang figured that Alameda owed FTX about $11 billion.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: A company owing another company billions of dollars indicates a significant financial entanglement.
> > Fact From Story: Wang and Bankman-Fried determined that about $8 billion in customer money was gone
> > > Fact From Story: FTX was not fine and assets were not fine because FTX did not have enough assets for customer withdrawals | Fact From Story
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Companies that do not have enough assets for customer withdrawals are at risk of going bankrupt. | Commonsense Knowledge
> > Commonsense Knowledge: If a company does not have enough assets for customer withdrawals, it is in a state of financial distress.
> Commonsense Knowledge: Paying lenders with customer funds is a misuse of funds.
